title: Signal DSP Processing Lab Demo

launch.notes: Runs the existing stretch, marker-analysis, and transform-artifact boundary descriptor and acceptance lanes, records one machine-readable receipt, and emits a rendered operator companion view.

scenarios.title: DSP Processing Lab Bootstrap
scenarios.summary: Captures bounded DSP processing meaning across stretch, marker-analysis, and transform-artifact proof surfaces through one repo-owned inspection surface.

evidence.notes: This bootstrap surface wraps the existing DSP boundary descriptors and acceptance lanes without inventing an editor shell, waveform browser, or tutorial UI.

known_exclusions: Analysis feature-inspector work remains deferred to later g09.013 planning decisions.
This surface proves DSP processing meaning through existing boundary families and does not claim editor, browser, or product-shell breadth.
This demo does not redesign DSP/runtime behavior; it reuses the existing proof surfaces.
expected_checks: The receipt captures machine-readable stretch, marker-analysis, and transform-artifact boundary descriptors.
The receipt records that the existing stretch, marker-analysis, and transform-artifact acceptance lanes completed successfully.
The rendered companion view makes the three DSP boundary families visually inspectable without reading raw JSON first.
The receipt keeps DSP processing meaning explicit instead of flattening the seam into a generic product demo.
signal-dsp, signal-dsp-resample, and signal-dsp-spectral only move to live demo coverage because this manifest and receipt exist.
